title: What Men Live By
text:
Simon, a poor village shoemaker, went to town one winter to buy sheepskins for a coat. His customers would not pay their debts, so he spent the little he had on vodka and set off home grumbling. Near a roadside shrine he found a young man sitting naked in the cold. Simon was afraid and almost passed by, but his conscience turned him back. He put his own coat on the stranger and brought him home.

His wife Matrena was furious at a drunk husband bringing home another mouth to feed. But when she looked at the stranger, pity rose in her, and she gave him the last of their bread. At that moment the stranger smiled for the first time.

His name was Michael. He stayed and worked as Simon's apprentice, and he worked wonderfully. He smiled a second time when a rich gentleman ordered boots to last a year, and Michael made soft slippers instead, the kind used for the dead; the gentleman died that very day. Years later a woman came in with two little girls, one of them lame, and told how she had taken them in when their mother died. Michael smiled a third time.

Then he revealed that he was an angel, punished for refusing to take that mother's soul, and sent to earth to learn three truths. He had learned that love dwells in people, that no one is given to know what he truly needs, and that people live not by care for themselves but by love.
lesson: None of us gets through life by our own planning alone. We live because others choose to care for us, so do the same for those around you.
people: Simon the shoemaker, his wife Matrena, the angel Michael
source: Leo Tolstoy, What Men Live By (1881)
